first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and inherited evidence indicates that shortening onboarding improves time-to-value and early adoption. Verify this directly, while also checking the durability and qualified-revenue economics of promotional pricing given the competitor threat. Run a guarded onboarding simplification test with qualified activation, retained usage, conversion, and revenue quality as success criteria so increased completion does not merely create low-value signups.

final.rationale: Run a standard, instrumented onboarding simplification experiment this week. The verified record shows shortened onboarding increased completion by 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention by 3%, directly addressing both current onboarding and activation declines. Signup simplification provides supporting evidence. Do not use promotional pricing: although it increased qualified revenue 18% initially, retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive the first renewal cycle. Evaluate activation, time-to-value, 30-day retention, renewal intent, and qualified revenue to ensure improved completion translates into sustainable value rather than lower-quality conversions.
